context: Measured 2026-11-26 from the corpus rule PR's CI fast-duration verdict and a local --durations profile.
description:
## Problem
The corpus rule change adds about 58 s of new fast-tier test time (CI-normalised, fast-duration verdict of CI run 45727559063). Three tests carry 31.2 s:
- tests/unit/core/results/test_corpus_rule.py::test_single_iteration_is_a_label_only_for_every_combination (12.6 s): for each of 11,424 fact combinations it loops over 2 x 5 inner cases and recomputes the baseline outcome and the public refusal inside the inner loop, so most rule calls repeat.
- tests/unit/scripts/test_corpus_compliance_snapshot.py::test_committed_corpus_matches_the_snapshot (9.8 s) and ::test_changing_the_rule_table_moves_the_snapshot (8.8 s): each derives outcomes for all stored bundles; the module fixture recomputes on every xdist worker.
The fast tier has an absolute ceiling (quality/fast-duration-ceiling.json); before the 2026-11-26 baseline refresh, develop's untimed tests already used 166 of the 170 s allowance, so every PR's fast-tier cost competes for the same headroom.

## Change
- Remove repeated work from the enumeration: compute each baseline once per row-count setting and each refusal once per iteration count, keeping every combination and every iteration count (None, 1, 2, 3, 4).
- For the whole-corpus snapshot tests: share one computation per session, or move them to the medium tier only if a required CI step on every PR that touches the rule still runs the snapshot check.

## Decision gates
- The enumerated combinations, the iteration boundary values and the snapshot comparison must stay exactly as strong; if a speed-up would drop any of them, do not make it.
- Moving a test out of the fast tier needs evidence that a required check still runs it on every relevant PR; otherwise stop and report.

## Verification rubric
- Mutation check: changing the single-iteration threshold (count < 3 to count < 2) still fails the enumeration test.
- The fast-duration verdict on the PR shows the new-test time for these files down by at least 20 s.

## Guardrails
- Reproduce or measure before changing anything; record the command, log path and run id in the item context.
- Fix the root cause. Never skip, xfail, loosen a check or bound, or raise a timeout only to make a test or run pass; a timing or limit change needs measured evidence and owner approval.
- No rule, check, label or test may name a platform or a version matrix unless the item is about that platform.
- Never edit stored result files under results-data/ or CHANGELOG.md; user-facing changes add a changelog.d fragment.
- No explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check); make duplicate-check-delta stays at +0; reuse existing helpers.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run after make heavy-status, with command, maximum run time and log path announced first. Never touch the lock or set BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT=force, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_WATCHDOG=off, or raise BENCHBOX_HEAVY_MEMORY_BUDGET_GIB. No live cloud runs.
- Work in a linked worktree; one pull request; run the local review before opening it; fix hosted-review findings. No stand-in approval unless the owner names the PR and head.
- Re-read paths and line numbers before editing and report drift instead of guessing.
- When a decision gate's stop condition is met, stop and report to the owner with the evidence; never substitute a different decision.
